annotation.authors_or_issuer: Skubis, I.; Wodarski, K.; Lütge, C.
key_provisions_or_claims: ChatGPT 3.5 declined to name virtual sex robot influencers when asked directly, citing responsible AI use.
Stating a scientific research purpose led it to answer partially, listing sex robot manufacturers instead.
Responses were evaluated for linguistic, social and ethical handling of sensitive topics.
Calls for continued improvement of AI ethical programming to balance informational accuracy with ethical integrity.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article analysing how ChatGPT 3.5 responds to prompts about sex robots, assessing linguistic handling, social implications and adherence to ethical guidelines. Finds the model refuses or partially answers sensitive requests depending on prompt framing, and calls for better ethical programming of generative AI. Sex robots are the topic, not the governed system.
annotation.title_clean: Human-ChatGPT interaction: prompt analysis on the basis of sex robots' topic – linguistic, social and ethical considerations of Generative AI
annotation.title_en: Human-ChatGPT interaction: prompt analysis on the basis of sex robots' topic – linguistic, social and ethical considerations of Generative AI
